name: Ambrosia Energy
summary: Builds off-grid solar-plus-battery plants for businesses that cannot wait for a grid connection; first West Texas site under construction in 2026.

name: Amca
summary: Re-engineers hard-to-source aerospace and defense components, including parts with long lead times or missing technical data.

name: Anduril Industries
summary: Autonomous defense systems tied together by its Lattice software; building Fury combat aircraft at its Arsenal-1 campus in Ohio.

name: Apex
summary: Mass-produces standardized satellite buses (power and propulsion) so customers can focus on payloads.

name: Arda
summary: Software that turns hardware designs into assembly plans and work instructions; used inside Anduril's manufacturing stack.

name: Astranis
summary: Small geostationary communications satellites dedicated to a single operator or government.

name: Atomic Industries
summary: Automates injection-mold design and production with physics simulation, supplying molded plastic parts.

name: Base Power
summary: Home batteries, built in Austin, that support the grid while keeping backup power for outages.

name: Castelion
summary: Low-cost hypersonic missiles meant to be bought in large numbers; building a production campus in New Mexico.

name: CHAOS Industries
summary: Distributed radar systems built from arrays of smaller antennas for early warning and precision tracking.

name: Chariot Defense
summary: Tactical power systems that keep drones, sensors and electronic-warfare gear running in the field.

name: Covenant
summary: Long-range precision-strike missile designed for mass production in the US, Germany and Israel.

name: CX2
summary: Electronic-warfare systems that locate and disrupt hostile radio signals, including drone links and jammers.

name: Diode
summary: Tools that let engineers write circuit board designs as code and get boards built with fewer supplier handoffs.

name: Forterra

name: Endurance Energy
summary: Modular generators that turn undersea hydrothermal heat into electricity for coastal grids.

name: Foundry Robotics
summary: Flexible robotic assembly cells that move hardware from prototype to production without a dedicated factory per product.

name: General Matter
summary: Building domestic HALEU uranium enrichment at Paducah, Kentucky, backed by a DOE award.

name: Generalist
summary: AI models that teach robots dexterous physical tasks from demonstrations.

name: Hadrian
summary: Highly automated precision machining factories for aerospace and defense programs.

name: Helsing
summary: AI-driven autonomous strike drones and aircraft, produced in distributed factories across allied countries.

name: Hermeus
summary: Uncrewed high-speed aircraft built through rapid prototype iteration; licensed to manufacture F100 engines.

name: Heron Power
summary: Solid-state power electronics that take over transformer functions for grid connections.

name: Impulse Space
summary: Orbital transfer vehicles that move spacecraft between orbits.

name: K2 Space
summary: Large, high-power satellites for communications and defense, built mostly in-house.

name: Mach Industries
summary: Unmanned strike aircraft and munitions with in-house propulsion and a retoolable factory network.

name: Mariana Minerals
summary: Automates mining and refining; owns a copper mine and refinery in Utah and is developing lithium in Texas.

name: Mind Robotics
summary: AI models and robot hardware for factory jobs that fixed automation struggles with, tested in Rivian plants.

name: Neros Technologies
summary: First-person-view attack and interceptor drones built on a supply chain it says avoids China.

name: Nominal
summary: Test and telemetry data platform for hardware teams, from prototype through production.

name: Northwood
summary: Ground-station antennas and network service for satellite operators.

name: Peak Energy
summary: Sodium-ion grid batteries that need less cooling; factory planned in Sacramento.

name: Perennial Autonomy
summary: Interceptor, reconnaissance and strike drones under a multi-year Pentagon procurement contract.

name: Podium Automation
summary: Designs and builds industrial control panels with its own software and automated wire processing.

name: Prometheus
summary: AI models for engineering design and simulation of complex hardware.

name: Radiant
summary: Factory-built, transportable 1 MW microreactors aimed at military bases and remote sites.

name: Redwood Materials
summary: Recycles used batteries and scrap into battery materials, and reuses EV packs for grid storage.

name: Relativity Space
summary: Developing the reusable Terran R launch vehicle.

name: Saronic Technologies
summary: Autonomous surface vessels for the Navy, plus a large new shipyard in Texas.

name: SendCutSend
summary: Instant-quote online service for laser-cut, machined, bent and welded custom parts.

name: Senra Systems
summary: Wire harnesses for aerospace and defense, run on its own engineering and production software.

name: Shield AI
summary: Hivemind autonomy software that flies aircraft without GPS or comms, plus the V-BAT drone.

name: Skydio
summary: Autonomous drones and docks for defense, infrastructure and public safety, built in California.

name: Specter
summary: Vision AI with mesh sensors and rugged edge compute for factories, infrastructure and logistics.

name: Stoke Space
summary: Fully reusable Nova launch vehicle, preparing for first launch from Cape Canaveral.

name: Ulysses
summary: Underwater robots and launch-and-recovery vessels for inspection and naval missions.

name: Unlimited Industries
summary: Software-driven design and construction of power and data infrastructure.

name: Valar Atomics
summary: Gas-cooled nuclear reactors and the processes to mass-manufacture them.

name: Varda
summary: Orbital factories that process pharmaceuticals in microgravity; reentry capsules also gather hypersonic flight data.

name: Westmag
summary: Manufactures drone motors and robot actuators in South San Francisco, targeting tens of millions of units a year.
